standing_bounds.authenticity_limit: The adopted semantics establish CONTENT INTEGRITY and PROVENANCE RECORDING only. They do not establish cryptographic authenticity (no signatures, no trust root exists in the repository) and they do not establish human authorization (a digest or a decided_by field is not a human). This limitation was stated to the User in the Round 12 decision interface and the User adopted the semantics WITH that understanding.
standing_bounds.fail_closed: Every adopted semantics fails closed: a missing timestamp, missing gate record, null digest, absent manifest, or undefined approval interaction is a failure or an UNIMPLEMENTED report, never a pass.
standing_bounds.gate_stays_read_only: The gate never writes approval state, never transitions the inventory, and never creates evidence. All adopted semantics are observational checks computed at gate-run time.

decisions.title: Adopt the six runtime-gate semantics designs (evidence-freshness, evidence-authenticity, cms-state-digest, p8-contract-digest, req-p10-07-reconciliation, approval-state-interaction)
decisions.decision: The six semantics designs presented in the Round 12 decision package (Part 2) are adopted as the repository's chosen semantics for the six currently-UNIMPLEMENTED runtime-gate controls. (1) evidence-freshness: evidence records carry generated_at (RFC 3339) and optional freshness_window_days; the gate compares against gate-run time; a missing timestamp FAILS; the window length itself is deferred to the first implementation grant. (2) evidence-authenticity: a gate-record JSON format (producing command, input digests, output digests, UTC timestamp, emitting tool version) whose claims the gate cross-checks by recomputing digests; contradiction FAILS; this is content-integrity plus provenance recording, NOT cryptographic authenticity. (3) cms-state-digest: canonical JSON (sorted keys, UTF-8, no insignificant whitespace) of the CMS state files, SHA-256, rendered sha256:<hex>; the gate recomputes and fails closed on mismatch or null. (4) p8-contract-digest: the same scheme over the P8 ContentType contract inputs, deliberately separate from (3) so a content edit does not invalidate the type contract and vice versa. (5) req-p10-07-reconciliation: a backend operation manifest to be created with the first backend code; the gate set-compares declared state_changing_operations against the manifest; a missing manifest FAILS (fail-closed); for the Home slice the empty-vs-empty case passes only when the manifest exists and is also empty. (6) approval-state-interaction: two distinct acts - contents approval (D-P10-8, in the decision ledger) and inventory approval (user_approval, set only by an authorized act, never by the gate); the transition COMPLETE_AWAITING_USER_APPROVAL to COMPLETE_VERIFIED_USER_APPROVED requires BOTH a full gate pass AND a set user_approval; per the User's APPROVAL-MECHANISM: OPTION A decision, a fresh explicit User approval act is required when the gate passes - D-P10-8's contents-approval does not carry over.
decisions.reason: The User adopted the semantics by the Round 12 decision line 'SEMANTICS: ADOPT', having been presented each design's purpose, I/O, algorithm, failure mode, positive/negative/tamper tests, migration path and limitations. The designs use only repository-verifiable primitives (stdlib hashlib/json), preserve fail-closed behavior, and keep the existence/integrity/provenance/authenticity/human-authorization distinctions explicit rather than collapsing them.
